title: Prescriptive Tuning Wizard — Sketch Notes and Backlog
content:
Purpose: quick sketches and grooming notes for a prescriptive tuning wizard that recommends (and optionally applies) batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles for a given workload. Goal is to reduce friction for devs who want a guided, safety-first flow that ties recommendations to cost/latency/QoR tradeoffs.

Audience: product PMs, PD designers, infra engineers, solutions engineers who will demo/apply these presets for customers. This is intentionally rough — prioritizing flow logic + edgecases over pixel-perfect visuals.

Key ideas and constraints (short):
- Start from a workload profile (sample requests, traffic histogram, latency SLO).
- Offer 3 modes: Explain-only, Suggest-and-Preview (safe simulation), and Apply (automated rollout + rollback hooks).
- Recommendations must surface expected cost delta, median p95 latency impact estimate, and a quick signal about quality risk (low/medium/high) with example prompt checks.
- Safety: quantization proposals are conservative by default (e.g., suggest int8 for large models only after a small eval set).
- UX should favor incremental opt-ins: patch-level application (route-level, model-version-level, or global policy).

User stories (prioritized):
1) As an SRE, I want to see which routes are most wasteful and get a one-click suggestion for batching and a simulated before/after latency curve. (OPT-9731)
2) As an ML engineer, I want to run a small QA sample to see quality drift after an int8 quantize suggestion before enabling it for production.
3) As a product owner, I want cost savings estimates and a simple rollback plan I can share with finance.

High-level flow (sketch):
- Entry: Console -> Optimize -> "Tuning Wizard". If user has a saved workload, auto-populate. Else, provide a simple collector: route selection + timeframe.
- Step 1: Analyze. Show traffic mix, tokens per request, median seq length, p50/p95 latency, current batching size distribution, cache hit rate. Visual: small stacked bars, histogram. Action: "Run quick profiler (30–120s)".
- Step 2: Recommendations. List cards for top suggestions: batching (change target batch size / batching window), caching (prefix caching enabled for identical prompts, KV policy), quantization (suggest model variant e.g., 13B-int8). Each card: expected delta (cost, latency), confidence score, quick evidence (sample requests affected). Buttons: Preview | Details | Apply.
- Step 3: Preview & Test. For each selection, allow: dry-run latency sim, apply to canary slice (% traffic), and run a tiny eval set (user-provided or auto-sampled). Show side-by-side generation examples.
- Step 4: Rollout. Guided canary/gradual rollout controls, automatic monitor hooks (QoR regression, latency > SLO), and rollback triggers.

Wireframe notes (visuals described for designer):
- Primary canvas: left column = workload summary, center = recommendation cards, right column = preview/test panel. Mobile not primary.
- Recommendation card anatomy: header w/ icon (batch/cache/quant), one-line suggestion, expected % cost change, expected p95 latency change, confidence pill (low/med/high), mini evidence line ("affects 18% of tokens"). CTA row: [Preview] [Apply w/ canary] (secondary ellipsis -> details).
- Preview panel: small simulated latency/time series (before/after), small table of sample prompts with generated output, a quality risk checklist (e.g., hallucination risk, tokenization/mismatch risk), a small toggle to "upgrade to conservative mode" which changes suggested quantization level and adds extra eval items.

Microcopy and messaging (important):
- Avoid promising absolute numbers: use language like "estimated" and include ranges.
- When recommending quantization, warn: "This suggestion reduces memory and cost but may slightly change output characteristics. Run the QA check before enabling for high-sensitivity routes."
- Use non-technical fallback copy for finance sharing: "Estimated monthly cost impact: -$5,200 (approx). Confidence: medium."

Backlog and grooming items (rough, with rough sizing):
- OPT-9740: Build lightweight profiler task that collects traffic histogram + sample set (2w)
- OPT-9741: Recommendation engine backend: heuristic rules + ML model for confidence estimates (3w)
- OPT-9742: UI components: recommendation card, preview panel, rollout controls (2w)
- OPT-9743: QA harness integration: run internal eval set and diff (1w)
- OPT-9744: Canary orchestration wiring + rollback hooks w/ SLO alarms (3w)
- OPT-9745: Autosave + shareable report export (pdf + share link) (1w)
- OPT-9746: E2E tests + staging demo (1w)

Edge cases & discussion notes (from meeting):
- Multi-model stacks: if customers use model routing, recommendations should surface which variants are safe to change and which are pinned. If pinned, suggest a fallback route instead of direct change.
- Small traffic customers: recommendations should gracefully degrade to "advice only" if there isn't enough telemetry for confident estimates.
- Privacy/PII: sample prompt capture must be scrubbed; present only token-level summaries or pseudo-samples except with explicit opt-in.
- Conflicting optimizations: batching can increase latency for low-traffic routes; UI needs to indicate per-route SLO conflicts and suggest per-route policies.

Early mock interactions (example flows):
- Demo flow A: "Reduce cost for low-priority routes"
  - Select routes: /summarize-news, /embed-search (low priority tag)
  - Wizard suggests: enable prefix caching on /summarize-news (est. -22% cost), set batch window=35ms for /embed-search (est. -18% cost but +15ms p95). Preview shows acceptable p95 for /embed-search when canaryed at 10% traffic.
- Demo flow B: "Aggressive model compression for bulk ingestion"
  - Suggests quantization for 70% of traffic to int8 variant, but flags high QoR risk for aggregation tasks. Recommends run-of-sample QA (provided by user).

Safety and rollout policy text (for compliance/legal review):
- Include an "approval required" toggle for enterprise customers that forces an admin sign-off before Apply.
- All applied changes generate audit logs with before/after config, timestamp, actor, and attached QA report.

Open questions (to resolve in next design sync):
- Do we expose the raw eval sample prompts in the UI (even if scrubbed) or only synthetic examples? (security/legal)
- What are default confidence thresholds for auto-suggest vs. only-show-advice?
- How to map recommendations to billing line-items exactly (token cost vs. infra savings)?

Next steps (owners & immediate action items):
- Rina: prototype recommendation card in Figma (due 2026-02-20)
- Ethan: spike on profiler sampling timeframe tradeoffs (due 2026-02-17)
- Sofia: draft user-facing microcopy and export template for the shareable report (due 2026-02-22)
- Leo: mock backend contract for applying canary & rollback API endpoints; coordinate with SRE (due 2026-02-24)

Notes-to-self: keep the wizard small at MLP — focus on 2 primary suggestions (batching + prefix caching) and surface quantization as an "advanced" path that requires an explicit QA run. Remove UI clutter: collapse low-confidence suggestions under "Other ideas".

Comments from last review meeting (2026-01-28):
- "We need clearer cost labeling — if we show dollars, show range and link to pricing explanation." — finance.
- "Can we support saved presets for customers to reuse recommended bundles?" — solutions-eng (login: SOL-1122)
- "Add a checkbox for 'do not touch pinned models' in tenant policies." — enterprise-sales

Attachments: rough ASCII wireframe sketches appended in Google Drive figma link above.

End of doc (for now) — will iterate after prototyping session.
summary: Rough sketch and backlog for a prescriptive tuning wizard that recommends batching, caching, and quantization with preview/test/canary flow. Includes user stories, flow, wireframe notes, backlog tickets, and next steps.
